page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.large is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8163 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, delivering 2 vCPUs from a single physical core via hyperthreading. Hardware resources include 4.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU), a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and hardware instruction support including AVX, AVX-512F, and AES. The instance features no bundled local storage and contains no discrete graphics accelerators.

Across standardized benchmarks, the instance yields performance typical of legacy entry-tier compute instances. Stress-ng scores reflect 1,101.79 in single-core and 1,461.5 in multi-core metrics, positioning it in lower percentiles. Geekbench results show 941.0 for single-core execution and 1,114.0 for multi-core throughput, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 1,823.49 and PassMark memory score of 926.98. In uncached large-block memory operations, read speeds register at 10.04 GB/sec and write speeds at 9.48 GB/sec.

Workload metrics indicate steady execution for modest network and compute tasks, recording 1.29 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and 1.51 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. For lightweight machine learning execution on a small 135M model, prompt processing registers at 115.52 tokens per second with text generation at 37.25 tokens per second. Resource constraints, specifically the 2 vCPU and 4.0 GB allocation alongside reliance on remote storage, trade off compute density for low-cost operational footprints. It functions best for lightweight front-end web services, basic CI/CD utility scripts, small caching instances, and non-critical microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.large is a compute-optimized instance offering 2 vCPUs and 4.0 GB of memory, driven by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor at 2.5 GHz on the KVM hypervisor. Featuring an x86_64 architecture with 1 physical core and 2 threads, it includes 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth and no local storage or GPUs. Benchmark outputs place compute and memory throughput in entry tiers, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 941.0, multi-core score of 1,114.0, PassMark CPU rating of 1,823.49, and 1.51 million Redis SET operations per second. Its qualitative value lies in low-overhead execution for tasks where large memory or disk IOPS are unnecessary. The instance is suited for lightweight web serving, small caching layers, microservices, and general CI/CD utilities.
